perspective:
Keith’s available information:

- He is a construction worker at a company where Elizabeth Sun is the receptionist; they have a friendly but professional relationship, mainly interacting when he visits the office for paperwork/project updates.
- Recently, he observed Elizabeth acting unusually curt/short with him over several days.
- He suspected he might have upset her through a misunderstanding or an unknown mistake.
- He asked Elizabeth if he had done something to upset her. She said no, that she was dealing with personal stuff, and apologized if she had seemed short.
- He felt sympathetic and offered to listen/support her, suggesting a coffee break. Elizabeth accepted and thanked him.
- During the coffee break, Elizabeth shared more about her personal stresses. Keith perceived them as severe.
- Keith thought professional help might benefit her, but worried about suggesting it without offending her.
- He told Elizabeth he appreciated her sharing and asked if she had considered talking to a professional, noting an external perspective can help. Elizabeth said she had thought about it but was unsure/hesitant about seeking help.
- Afterward, Keith observed Elizabeth become slightly withdrawn. He believed his suggestion might have embarrassed her and felt regretful.
- He told her he hoped he hadn’t overstepped and that he was there to support her no matter what. Elizabeth said he hadn’t overstepped, appreciated his concern, and said it was just a lot to think about.
- Later, Keith perceived Elizabeth as more open and appreciative of his concern. He believed she valued his support and felt more comfortable around him.
- He told her he was glad they talked and that he is always available if she needs to chat or take a break. Elizabeth thanked him, said it meant a lot, and that she felt better knowing she had his support.
- Keith intends to maintain this supportive relationship.
